summary: Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry lists visa-free stays of up to 30 days for ordinary passport holders from the EU, the US, the UK, China and many other countries, and up to 90 days for citizens of several neighbouring states including Russia, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan. Citizens of the states on its e-Visa list can get a single-entry tourist eVisa through the Visa-Migration Portal on an invitation from the Kazakh side.

fee.notes: The Foreign Ministry's e-visa page gives a consular fee of US$60 for the single-entry tourist eVisa (US$80 for business and medical eVisas). The same page says an eVisa is issued on an invitation from the Kazakh side, that paid consular fees are not refundable, that you may enter and leave Kazakhstan on an eVisa only through the checkpoints of the international airports of Nur-Sultan and Almaty (the Embassy in Washington's January 2026 QazETA notice says only through border crossing points of the international airports of Kazakhstan), and that you must carry a printed copy of the eVisa at the border and during your stay. It also says an eVisa is valid only for its recipient and does not cover accompanying persons.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan — E-visa of the Republic of Kazakhstan

vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. WHO records no minimum age for Kazakhstan, and any transit through such a country's airport counts, however short the stop.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states whether travel insurance is required to enter Kazakhstan. The UK Foreign Office says the medical facilities in Kazakhstan are not as advanced as in the UK and tells travellers to make sure they have adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds to cover the cost of medical treatment or evacuation by air ambulance and repatriation.

declarations.text: Your hotel or the person hosting you must register your arrival with the Kazakh authorities within 3 working days of your arrival. If you stay privately, make sure your host does it.

currencyLimits.text: Cash worth more than US$10,000 must be declared to customs on arrival. Foreign-currency cash worth more than US$10,000 may not be taken out of the country; a larger declared amount can be exported only in tenge.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says robberies are uncommon in cities and rural areas but do happen, advises against walking alone at night and using unofficial taxis, and recommends licensed, pre-ordered taxi services instead of flagging taxis down.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says your hotel or the person hosting you must register your arrival with the Kazakh authorities within 3 working days. If you stay in a private apartment, make sure your host does it.
The UK Foreign Office advises against flagging down taxis and recommends licensed, pre-ordered taxi services to avoid unlicensed cabs and overcharging.
Kazakh is the state language, and the Constitution says Russian is officially used alongside it in state bodies.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Kazakhstan?
faq.answer: Ordinary passport holders from the EU states, the US, the UK, Canada, Japan, China and many other countries enter visa-free for up to 30 days, per the Foreign Ministry's visa-regime table; citizens of Russia, Belarus, Ukraine, Moldova, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Mongolia and Turkey, among others, get up to 90 days. Citizens of the states on the e-Visa list can get a tourist eVisa on the Visa-Migration Portal with an invitation from the Kazakh side.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Kazakhstan visa-free?
faq.answer: The Foreign Ministry's visa-regime table gives ordinary passport holders of the EU states, the US, the UK and China up to 30 days. Some allowances differ: up to 90 days for several neighbouring states and for Albania, Andorra, Saint Kitts and Nevis, San Marino and Turkey, 60 days for the Dominican Republic, 28 days for Barbados, and 14 days for India, Iran, Hong Kong and Macau. The UK government's travel advice adds, for British nationals, a limit of 90 days without a visa in any 180-day period.

faq.question: Do I need to register after arriving in Kazakhstan?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says your hotel or the person hosting you must register your arrival with the Kazakh authorities within 3 working days. The Foreign Ministry says holders of valid electronic visas are exempt from registration with the migration authorities.

faq.question: How does the Kazakhstan eVisa work?
faq.answer: Eligible nationalities apply online at the Visa-Migration Portal (vmp.gov.kz) for a single-entry tourist eVisa for a consular fee of US$60, on the strength of an invitation from the Kazakh side. It allows a stay of up to 30 days, and the Foreign Ministry's e-visa page says that eVisa holders may enter and leave Kazakhstan only through the checkpoints of the international airports of Nur-Sultan and Almaty; the Embassy in Washington's January 2026 notice says only through border crossing points of the international airports of Kazakhstan.

faq.question: Can Russian and other CIS citizens enter Kazakhstan without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes. The Foreign Ministry's visa-regime table lists visa-free stays of up to 90 days for ordinary passport holders of Russia, Belarus, Ukraine, Moldova, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan; for Armenia and Azerbaijan it gives 90 days within 180 days.
